pageCache.text:
British Values
At Weston Park, we aim to actively promote British values to ensure all of our children leave school prepared for their new secondary school, and for life in modern Britain.
Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that different people may have different views and opinions.
We teach our pupils about
• democracy • rule of law • individual liberty • mutual respect • having tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values | Weston Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision & Values Statement
‘Achieving Together, Growing Together’
At Weston Park we are a welcoming community who support our children to have the confidence, independence and courage to fulfil their potential. We teach children to value fairness and diversity and to care for themselves and others.
Through our rich, creative and ambitious curriculum, we aim to foster an enthusiasm for learning, and to empower and inspire our children to make positive change in the world with their words and actions.
Alongside our Good Habits of Learning – being curious, imaginative, disciplined, resilient and collaborative learners, we teach these core values through our curriculum:
Respect: we value each other for who we are, even when we disagree
Responsibility: we think about how our actions affect others and understand the consequences of what we do
Kindness: we are considerate and supportive of each other’s feelings
Community: we appreciate the strength and value of being together and working with others
Integrity: we are honest and act according to our values, even when it is challenging
Equality: we believe that everyone should have a fair opportunity to make the most of their lives and talents
Courage: we are not afraid to challenge, ask questions and stand up for what we think is right
Vision and Values

Welcome
Welcome to Weston Park Primary School.
Weston Park is a small, single form entry, primary school in the heart of North London. We welcome children and families from a variety of different backgrounds and cultures and we celebrate the differences we have. Together, staff, parents and children help to make Weston Park a vibrant and exciting place to learn, where the curriculum is enriched with a variety of educational visits, workshops in school and extra curricular activities.
We encourage our children to strive for excellence now and in the future in all they do. From the moment children start school we aim to inspire them to learn and to enjoy learning through our broad based and engaging curriculum. Each child is inspired to use their imagination and curiosity and to work collaboratively to solve problems and propose solutions. We help our children to appreciate the impact that their behaviour has on themselves and others and to work together to preserve our safe and disciplined school environment.
We aim to be a centre of excellence at the heart of our diverse community, giving each child the fundamental knowledge, skills and dispositions they need to reach their full potential and to become responsible, caring and resilient future citizens.
I hope that you are able to find all the information you need on the website and if you have any further questions about the school please feel free to contact us and we will get back to you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast and After School Club | Weston Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Club
Weston Park offers a breakfast club and an after school club which provides good quality care and provision for the children from Nursery to Year 6.
Our Breakfast Club provides a safe, secure environment before school, where Weston Park children can have breakfast, relax or play.
The children are supervised by two members of staff. We offer a healthy breakfast of toast or cereal, milk or juice.
Activities on offer include playing games, creative activities (drawing and making), lego and there is a quiet zone for reading. We are based in Kandinsky classroom and the children have access to the junior playground.
When Breakfast Club ends at 8.50am, the KS1 children are accompanied to their classrooms whilst KS2 children may join their friends in the playground.
Sessions cost £6.00 and must be booked and paid for in advance, using the online booking system. Any cancellations need 24 hours notice otherwise you will be charged. Please contact Mark in the school office for further details.
Our club is fun, friendly and packed full of activities, providing a safe environment for children when parents are working.
The club is supervised by three members of staff who collect the children from their class at the end of the school day.
We offer the children a wide range of activities both indoor and out, depending on the weather. Activities may include football, table tennis, painting, card making, drawing, sewing, board games, model building, badminton and a quiet area for reading or relaxation.
We are based in the school hall or the Kandinsky classroom and the children also have access to the playground as well.
Sessions cost £17.00 which includes a hot, light two course meal. If you prefer, you can supply your child with their own snack.
Sessions must be booked and paid for in advance, using the online booking system. Any cancellations need 24 hours notice otherwise you will be charged. Please contact Mark in the school office for further details.

pageCache.pageTitle: Current Governors | Weston Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Current Governors
George Ruiz - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 22 April 2024 to 21 April 2028
I joined the Governing Body in May 2020. I have been a resident of Crouch End for nearly thirty years and am a Chartered Accountant. I have extensive experience in senior financial leadership positions in the not-for-profit, Retail and Financial Service sectors. Specific areas of specialism include strategic planning, risk management and financial control.
2025-2026 responsibilities: Chair of Governing Body, member of People & Resources Committee
Kylie Agbim - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 7 Dec 2023 to 6 Dec 2027
I joined the governing body in February 2020 as a Parent Governor. I sit on the Children’s Committee. Two of my children attend the school and another is a former pupil. My background is in social policy and social work. I project managed a neighbourhood renewal programme aimed at raising attainment and tackling social inequalities in West London. In my spare time I enjoy tennis, cycling, singing and theatre. I am passionate about improving opportunities for all young people.
2025-2026 responsibilities: Vice-chair of Governing Body, Chair of Children’s Committee, Chair of Pay Committee, Racial Equity link governor
Lisa Fowler - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 30 May 2025 to 29 May 2029
I joined the governing body in September 2021. My career has been in Human Resources within Financial Services, and a key part of my experience has been focussed on wellbeing initiatives. I have also always had a passion for learning and supporting others with their learning.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of People & Resources Committee, Wellbeing and Medical Needs governor
Cailin Murphy - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 4 Jul 2024 to 3 Jul 2028
I joined the governing body in September 2020. My background is in analysis and strategy, and I am now a data scientist in the Civil Service. I am passionate about educational opportunity and have experience working in the broader education sector, including at the Department for Education and at a university.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of Children's Committee, Communications link governor, SEND link governor
Michelle O'Brien - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 1 April 2023 to 31 Mar 2027
I was an Associate Governor for nearly two years on the Pay & Resources Committee before being elected as a Parent Governor in July 2021. One of my children currently attends the school and is in KS2; my other child has now left Weston Park and is at secondary school. My background is in corporate social responsibility and the charitable sector and, in particular, delivering education programmes. I am currently in a grant-making role as Head of Charitable Partnerships at a London livery company focusing on grants supporting primary age numeracy and literacy as well as the criminal justice sector. I am particularly interested in evidence-based interventions and ensuring no child’s success is limited by their socio-economic background. In my spare time I enjoy swimming at the Crouch End lido and Hampstead Heath bathing pools.
2025-2026 responsibilities: Chair of People & Resources Committee, member of Pay Committee
Karan Singh - Local Authority Governor
Term of office from 22 Sep 2022 to 21 Sep 2026
I was appointed as a governor in autumn 2022. It was the opportunity to support the development of local children and the community that attracted me to the governor role. Within the last year I have both moved into Crouch End and become a father. My experience is in finance, initially qualifying as a chartered accountant before spending the last 9 years working as an investment analyst and most recently as a portfolio manager in the asset management industry. When time permits, I enjoy watching and playing cricket and seeing live music.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of People & Resources Committee, member of Pay Committee, Health & Safety link governor
Simone Vibert - Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 24 May 2022 to 23 May 2026
I joined the governing body in May 2022. My background is in children's policy, working across a broad range of issues. I started my career working for an autism charity and I now lead policy and research for an online safety charity. I am very proud to be working with everyone in the fantastic Weston Park community to make the school as good as it can possibly be. In my spare time I am a keen runner, cyclist and cinema-goer.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of Children’s Committee, Safeguarding link governor
Soozii Lim - Parent Governor
Term of office from 7 Dec 2023 to 6 Dec 2027
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of Children's Committee; EYFS link governor
Tim Lockie - Parent Governor
Term of office from 7 Dec 2023 to 6 Dec 2027
My name is Tim Lockie and my daughter, Phaedra, is currently in year 6 at the school. She has been at the school since Reception. I work as a full time NHS consultant cardiologist at the Royal Free Hospital where I am currently the clinical director. Ever since Phaedra started at the school, we have been hugely impressed with the manner in which the school has been run, especially during the challenging times of Covid where the pastoral care and leadership shown by all the staff members was extraordinary. We are proud to be a part of such a wonderful community and I am lucky that as parental governor I am to give something back to this very special place. I enjoy swimming in the lido and playing tennis (badly) in Stationers park to relax.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of People & Resources Committee
Soozii Lim - Parent Governor
Term of office from 7 Dec 2023 to 6 Dec 2027
I joined the governing body as a parent governor in December 2023. Both my children attend Weston Park Primary and love being part of its community.
My background is in teaching and leadership as an Assistant Head and SENDCo at a primary school in Hackney, giving me first-hand experience in both the joys of working in education, as well as the strategic and operational responsibilities the school has towards its pupils, families and staff.
We’ve always had really positive experiences as parents of the school and I wanted to combine my experiences working in education, and as a parent and support the school more widely.
Oliver Black-Hawkins: Co-opted Governor
Term of office from 20 Mar 2025 to 19 Mar 2029
I joined the governing body in March 2025 after five years volunteering as a student mentor at other local schools in the area. I work in management consulting with a focus on strategy and analysis for government and financial services. I’m from a big family of teachers and have always been passionate about education, so I am excited by the opportunity to use my skills to support the development of children in my local community, where I’ve lived for almost 10 years now. In my spare time I enjoy movies, live music and travel.
2025-2026 responsibilities: member of Children's Committee; Parent Engagement link governor

Some cookies are necessary in order to make this website function correctly. These are set by default and whilst you can block or delete them by changing your browser settings, some functionality such as being able to log in to the website will not work if you do this. The necessary cookies set on this website are as follows:
Website CMS
A 'sessionid' token is required for logging in to the website and a 'crfstoken' token is used to prevent cross site request forgery. An 'alertDismissed' token is used to prevent certain alerts from re-appearing if they have been dismissed. An 'awsUploads' object is used to facilitate file uploads.
Matomo
We use Matomo cookies to improve the website performance by capturing information such as browser and device types. The data from this cookie is anonymised.
reCaptcha
Cookies are used to help distinguish between humans and bots on contact forms on this website.
Cookie notice
A cookie is used to store your cookie preferences for this website.
